script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 10. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

The cells in your body are built from food you ate.  That apple, that sandwich, that salad—their molecules were disassembled and reassembled into you.  You are literally constructed from what you consume.

Digestion breaks food into basic molecules: amino acids, fatty acids, sugars. These are absorbed into your blood and distributed to cells. Your cells then reassemble these blocks into new proteins, membranes, and structures. Same blocks, new you. Your body replaces most of its cells over 7-10 years.  Skin cells last weeks, red blood cells months, bone cells years.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Inputs become outputs.  What you take in shapes what you become—literally, with food.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Input Awareness - Choose What Becomes You.

Here's your activity: At your next meal, consider: these molecules will be disassembled and rebuilt into my body. Does that change what you want to eat? Then expand the thought: what other 'inputs'—information, media, relationships—are shaping who you become? This helps you connect inputs to their effects on who you become.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how food becomes you can be applied to input awareness - choose what becomes you. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
